cards.explanation: The answer is mercy, friends. David says he lifts his voice to the LORD "for mercy" (Psalm 142:1). He isn't coming with a list of demands or a speech about how deserving he is. He just asks, loud and plain, from the cave.

The answer is False. David says, "I pour out my complaint before Him; I reveal my trouble to Him." (Psalm 142:2). He reveals his trouble to the LORD instead of hiding it. I think that's a pretty honest way to pray.

The answer is True, friends! David says, "Although my spirit grows faint within me, You know my way." (Psalm 142:3). His spirit is fading, but he still knows one thing for sure. I think that's a good thing to hold onto when you're running low.
The answer is a snare, friends. David says, "Along the path I travel they have hidden a snare for me." (Psalm 142:3). A snare is a trap. And he tells us it was hidden along his path.

The answer is no one attending to him. David says, "Look to my right and see; no one attends to me." (Psalm 142:4). He tells the LORD to look, and what he says is that no one attends to him. I think that sounds lonely.

The answer is False. David says, "There is no refuge for me; no one cares for my soul." (Psalm 142:4). Nobody around him cares for his soul. That is a heavy thing to say out loud, and he says it straight to the LORD.

The answer is refuge, friends! David cries to the LORD, "You are my refuge, my portion in the land of the living." (Psalm 142:5). A moment ago he said there was no refuge for him (Psalm 142:4). Now he says the LORD is his. A refuge is a safe place to run to.
The answer is strong. David says, "Rescue me from my pursuers, for they are too strong for me." (Psalm 142:6). He doesn't pretend he can handle them. He says it plainly and asks the LORD to step in.

The answer is prison, friends. David asks, "Free my soul from prison…" (Psalm 142:7). He's praying from a cave, and I think that word shows how shut in he feels. He wants out, and he asks the LORD to do the freeing.

The answer is praise, friends! David asks, "Free my soul from prison, that I may praise Your name." (Psalm 142:7). He doesn't only want out for his own sake. He tells the LORD what he plans to do once he's free.

The answer is the righteous, friends. David says, "The righteous will gather around me because of Your goodness to me." (Psalm 142:7). Earlier he said no one attended to him on his right (Psalm 142:4). Now he talks about people gathering around him. That's a big turn from a lonely cave.

The answer is True, friends! David says, "The righteous will gather around me because of Your goodness to me." (Psalm 142:7). He doesn't give the credit to himself. He points it to the LORD's goodness, and that's a fine way to end a cave prayer.
